agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider permissive property tax exemptions for 2027-2029
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider approving permissive property tax exemptions for 2027, 2028 and 2029, covering 168 properties (26 exempt by default, 142 approved applications). The bylaw must be adopted by October 31, 2026 and submitted to BC Assessment by November 1, 2026. Applications closed June 30, 2026. Four properties are recommended for rejection and four will see changed exemption status. Council reviews the list and policy on September 22, 2026, with final adoption set for October 27, 2026.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Check the proposed exemption list to see if your property is included, and watch for Council's decision on September 22, 2026.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to vote on adding Langley to Metro West business licence program
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider adopting two bylaws (Bylaw No. 14851 and Bylaw No. 14852) that would add the Township of Langley to the Metro West Inter-Municipal Business Licence (IMBL) program, expanding it from six to seven municipalities. The IMBL covers construction trades, building maintenance/repair/inspection contractors, and in-home health care providers. The annual IMBL fee stays at $300, and existing holders renewing for 2027 are automatically authorized to work in Langley — no new application needed. The expansion takes effect January 1, 2027, if all participating councils approve.
agenda_briefs.action_required: If you hold a Metro West IMBL, no action is needed — your 2027 renewal will automatically cover Langley; otherwise check your eligibility before the January 1, 2027 start.

key_dates.label: Burnaby Council vote on Metro West IMBL Langley expansion

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider forwarding Riverbend Court mezzanine rezoning
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider forwarding Rezoning Application REZ #26-10 for 8315 Riverbend Court to First and Second Reading at a future meeting. The application, by Open Space Architecture Inc., would rezone the site from CD Comprehensive Development District to I1 Industrial District to add 115 m2 of mezzanine floor area for workstations. Staff recommend skipping a public hearing because the application is consistent with the Official Community Plan. Final adoption requires a Site Disclosure Statement, Ministry of Transportation and Transit approval, and two new Class A bicycle parking spaces.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the future Council meeting where this rezoning is read; no public hearing is planned, so submit any concerns to Council before then.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider funding three bus shelter murals in Burnaby
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider approving $8,568 from the 2026 Anti-Graffiti Mural Grant Program to pay Astrographic Industries for vinyl murals at three bus shelters: eastbound Kingsway at Patterson Avenue, northbound Canada Way at Wedgewood Street, and northbound Gilmore Way at Sanderson Way. The artwork, "City Park" by Ebony Janson, is intended to deter graffiti and protect glass panels. The funding uses all remaining program money after an artist withdrew from the Kensington Overpass South mural.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to vote on contract for mixed waste metals recycling
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will vote on awarding a recycling services contract for mixed waste metals to Richmond Steel Recycling Ltd., with an estimated total revenue of $670,000 CAD including tax. The contract runs from October 1, 2026 to September 30, 2028, with an option to renew for three additional one-year terms. Final revenue will depend on the actual quantity of scrap metal recycled and the commodity pricing index. The city collected mixed metals at the Eco Centre through resident drop-offs and large item collections.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to vote on contract change for Burnaby Mountain water supply
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider approving a $260,373 (including tax) contract change to Stantec Consulting Ltd. for the Curtis-Duthie Burnaby Mountain Water Supply Improvements project (EA-3287). The change covers design, tender, contract administration and inspection of an additional 350mm watermain with communication ducts on Curtis Street and Burnaby Mountain Parkway, plus an additional pump at Aldrin pump station. This brings the total estimated contract value to $891,013, a 46.4% increase over the original $608,649 award.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision on this contract change if you do business with the city or work in construction.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider social purpose business in Burnaby strategy
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will vote on September 22, 2026 on a Social Planning Committee recommendation to recognize social purpose business as contributing to the City's social, economic and environmental objectives, and to direct staff to review incorporating it into the Social Sustainability Strategy and the Economic Development Strategy. The push comes from the Canadian Purpose Economy Project, which notes 38% of Canadian small and mid-sized businesses have or plan a social purpose. No new rules or fees are proposed yet.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch the September 22, 2026 Council vote on recognizing social purpose business in Burnaby's strategies.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to review preliminary cost impacts of upcoming PST changes
agenda_briefs.summary: BC's PST expansion takes effect October 1, 2026, applying 7% tax to accounting, architectural, engineering, geoscience, security, private investigation, and non-residential real estate services (including rental property and strata management). For architectural, engineering and geoscience services, PST applies to only 30% of the purchase price. Burnaby staff estimate the city's added costs at roughly $1,249,000 — about $757,674 for engineering/geoscience/architecture and $490,520 for accounting and security. Council will receive the report for information on September 22, 2026.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider Burnaby inter-municipal business licence bylaw
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to consider Bylaw #14851, which would join Burnaby to an inter-municipal business licence scheme with Delta, New Westminster, Richmond, Surrey, Vancouver and Langley. Eligible businesses — construction trades and related professionals, maintenance/repair/inspection contractors, and health care providers who visit clients at home — would pay a $300 annual fee to their home city and could then operate in all participating cities without buying separate licences. The fee is not pro-rated and is separate from any local licence fee. The bylaw is tied to a report going to Council on September 22, 2026, and is only at first reading.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch the September 22, 2026 Council meeting to see whether the report and bylaw move forward, since it could change how you licence your business across cities.

agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to vote on a proposed zoning amendment (Bylaw No. 10, 2026, REZ #24-23) for 3900 Grand Promenade, 9850 Austin Rd., and 9858 & 9898 Gatineau Place. agenda_briefs.title: Council to vote on Burnaby fee changes for January 2027
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council has adopted Amendment Bylaw No. 14850, which replaces dozens of fee schedules in the Burnaby Consolidated Fees and Charges Bylaw effective January 1, 2027. Business licence fees are set by category: for example, a cannabis store pays $5,378 for both initial and renewal licences, adult services pay $4,829, contractors pay $392 initial and $138 renewal, and most general businesses pay $691 initial and $208 renewal. Dog licences rise to $73 (unaltered) or $38 (spayed/neutered) if paid by March 1, and more after.
